newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares end up as Congress, UF agree to meet.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares end up as Congress, UF agree to meet.

text.p: Delhi shares closed higher on Wednesday, boosted by prospects of a meeting between the ruling United Front (UF) coalition and the Congress party to end the current political stalemate, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index closed 13.12 points higher at 766.52 points.

"If the outcome of the meeting between the government and Congress party is favourable then the market should witness a sharp rally in the coming sessions," said Shyam Bhatia of brokers Vashisht Securities.
The UF sent a formal letter to the Congress party on Wednesday to start talks aimed at resolving the 11-day-old political crisis, raising expectations of an agreement to avert mid-term polls.
News that the two sides were preparing for talks raised hopes that the investor-friendly budget for 1997/98 (April-March), presented in February, would also be approved by the parliament.
The budget, which would slash corporate and personal income tax rates, has been held hostage by political uncertainty.

Congress president Sitaram Kesri sparked the crisis on March 30 when he announced the withdrawal of his party's make-or-break support for Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's minority centre-left coalition.
Reliance Industries ended 4.60 rupees higher at 273.60 on speculative buying, brokers said.
State Bank of India gained 11.00 rupees to end at 283.95.
Larsen and Toubro closed 6.70 rupees higher at 215.80.
